messages:
carla: Heads up — canary rollout for model v44 is showing ~6% of requests still hitting v43. Config says traffic_split=5% -> v44. Anyone else?

ben: Reported by a customer and our internal smoke tests. Logs look like header-based routing and sticky cookie are disagreeing.

carla: Yep. Repro: curl with X-Client-Id and no cookie vs same client with session cookie gives different variants.

alice: I pushed the canary guard patch earlier that changed the rollout salt. Could be a hashing mismatch between header hashing and cookie hashing.

ben: Current routing snippet from config: 
```
traffic:
  - percent: 5
    variant: v44
guard:
  sticky_cookie: session_id
  header_hash: X-Client-Id
hash_fn: cityhash64
salt: 'rollout-salt-v2'
```

dima: If some nodes still have 'rollout-salt-v1' and others 'rollout-salt-v2' then the same client id will map to different buckets depending on which router handles the request. That would explain flips.

alice: Logs look exactly like that. Example: 
```
[2026-02-12T12:03:11Z] req id=abcd client=abc123 header_hash=42 cookie_hash=127 selected=v43
[2026-02-12T12:03:11Z] req id=abce client=abc123 header_hash=42 cookie_hash=42  selected=v44
```

ben: So some requests are deciding by header-hash (new salt) and others by cookie-hash (old salt). Same client, different variant. Not good for session consistency.

carla: Impact: sessions see inconsistent model behavior across sequential requests -> subtle UX regressions. Temporary mitigation idea: prefer cookie stickiness when both cookie and header are present.

dima: Quick mitigation is doable: compute both (old + new) hashes and accept either mapping during the transition. We'll need to store salt versions in rollout metadata. Can we hotfix?

alice: I can roll a hotfix to routing that checks dual salts (new + legacy) for the canary namespace behind a feature flag. Small CPU hit but should drop flip-rate quickly.

carla: Action items: alice -> push hotfix feature-flagged; ben -> observe canary metrics and flip-rate; dima -> prepare rollback plan and coord with infra to stop further salt churn. I'll notify support/customer.

deploy-bot: deploy started for eng-platform/routing:hotfix-dualhash by alice (rev ab12) — 1/3 nodes updated.

ben: After two nodes are updated the flip rate dropped to ~0.4% :tada: — monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood/instrumentation/rollouts/1829992468

carla: Follow-up: PR to version salt in rollout manifests, add unit/integration tests for mixed-salt scenarios, and update rollout UI to show salt version. Also add an alert for >1% flip-rate during rollouts.

carla: Note for postmortem: avoid changing core hashing salt while a rollout is in-flight; include migration path in rollout playbook.

ben: Good call. I'll draft the short incident blurb.

alice: Hotfix fully rolled. Will open PR for the compatibility layer and tests.

carla: Thanks everyone.
